terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase, “to say things that fight each other”. Pugnantia in this sense is classical (Hor. S. 1.1.103, pugnantia sēcum … compōnere, Lewis & Short s.v. compōnō); the phrase with loquī was not found in Lewis & Short or the loci.

sources: Lewis & Short: pugno · Lewis & Short: loquor
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 95, checked against the searchable text and the page images of the book.: p. 296.
